name: Nigeria
triviaFact: The most populous nation on the continent, renowned as the global powerhouse of the Nollywood cinema industry and Afrobeat musical revolutions.

name: Nicaragua
triviaFact: Features a vast freshwater inland lake harboring oceanic bull sharks and Ometepe, an hourglass island formed by two conjoined volcanoes rising from the waves.

name: Niue
triviaFact: Known as the Rock of Polynesia, this massive raised coral atoll became the world's first whole nation designated as an International Dark Sky Sanctuary.

name: Netherlands
triviaFact: A low-lying maritime marvel where over a quarter of the land sits below sea level, protected by the Delta Works engineering marvel and crisscrossed by historic canals and windmills.

name: Norway
triviaFact: Carved by monumental glacial fjords like Geirangerfjord and Nærøyfjord, where wooden stave churches date to the Viking Age and mountain plateaus shelter the world's sovereign wealth reserve.

name: Nepal
triviaFact: Home to eight of the world ten tallest peaks including Mount Everest, alongside historic pagoda-filled royal Durbar squares framed by the Himalayas.

name: Nauru
triviaFact: The smallest independent island republic on the planet, consisting of a single raised phosphate limestone atoll encircling central Buada Lagoon.

name: New Zealand
aliases: Land of the Long White Cloud
triviaFact: Renowned for the majestic glacial sounds of Fiordland, geothermal wonders in Rotorua, and endemic flightless kiwi birds thriving across ancient temperate rainforests.

name: Oman
triviaFact: An ancient seafaring sultanate on the Arabian Sea, renowned for historic mudbrick fortresses like Bahla, dramatic mountain wadis, and aromatic frankincense groves in Dhofar.

name: Pakistan
triviaFact: Cradles the ancient bronze age settlements of Mohenjo-daro and Harappa along the Indus River, crowned in the north by K2 and the dramatic Karakoram Highway.

name: Panama
triviaFact: An intercontinental isthmus bridged by an eighty-kilometer marvel of civil engineering that lifts interoceanic cargo vessels across continental divides via lock gates.

name: Pitcairn Islands
officialName: Pitcairn, Henderson, Ducie and Oeno Islands
triviaFact: The least populated jurisdiction on Earth with fewer than fifty residents, settled in 1790 by mutineers from HMS Bounty led by Fletcher Christian.

name: Peru
triviaFact: Heartland of the ancient Inca realm, where dry-stone citadel terraces crown mountain ridges in cloud forests above mysterious desert geoglyphs etched in arid plains.

name: Philippines
triviaFact: An archipelago of over seven thousand tropical islands, acclaimed for hand-carved two-thousand-year-old rice terraces in Banaue and subterranean underground rivers in Palawan.

name: Palau
triviaFact: Pioneered the world's first national shark sanctuary and ecological conservation pledge, renowned for mushroom-shaped limestone Rock Islands and Jellyfish Lake.

name: Papua New Guinea
officialName: Independent State of Papua New Guinea
triviaFact: The most linguistically diverse country on Earth with over 800 distinct living indigenous languages, blanketed by rugged highlands and primeval rainforests.

name: Poland
triviaFact: Restored its historic capitals with meticulous fidelity, from the Renaissance market square in Krakow to the underground cathedral chambers sculpted entirely of rock salt at Wieliczka.

name: Puerto Rico
triviaFact: Contains El Yunque—the only tropical rainforest in the United States National Forest System—and bioluminescent bays teeming with glowing dinoflagellates.

name: North Korea
triviaFact: A secluded socialist republic framed by the granite spires of Mount Kumgang and sacred Mount Paektu, centered on massive public squares and monumental statues of eternal leaders.

name: Portugal
triviaFact: The oldest nation-state on the Iberian Peninsula, famed for Manueline maritime architecture, blue azulejo ceramic tiles, soulful fado melodies, and port wine terraces along the Douro.

name: Paraguay
triviaFact: A bilingual inland nation where an indigenous language holds equal constitutional status and majority conversational dominance alongside Spanish throughout modern society.

name: Palestine
triviaFact: Contains ancient terraced olive groves in the Judean Hills and Jericho, widely recognized as one of the oldest continuously inhabited settlements in human history.

name: French Polynesia
triviaFact: Comprises 118 dispersed atolls and volcanic islands across five archipelagos, renowned for overwater bungalows in Bora Bora and legendary heavy surf breaks at Teahupo'o.

name: Qatar
triviaFact: A desert peninsula jutting into the Persian Gulf, distinguished by the futuristic skyline of West Bay, traditional dhow harbors, and I.M. Pei's Museum of Islamic Art.

name: Réunion
triviaFact: An Indian Ocean volcanic island dominated by the towering caldera of Piton de la Fournaise, one of the most consistently active shield volcanoes in the world.

name: Romania
triviaFact: Encompasses the wild Carpathian peaks sheltering Europe's largest brown bear population, Transylvanian fortified churches, and the mammoth marble Palace of the Parliament.

name: Russia
triviaFact: The largest country by land area, spanning eleven time zones from Baltic amber shores across Siberian taiga to Lake Baikal, the deepest and oldest freshwater lake on Earth.

name: Rwanda
triviaFact: Known as the Land of a Thousand Hills, celebrated for pioneering conservation of endangered mountain gorillas in Volcanoes National Park and high rates of female parliamentary representation.

name: Saudi Arabia
triviaFact: Cradle of Islam containing the holy cities of Mecca and Medina, home to the vast sand dunes of the Rub' al Khali and monumental rock-cut Nabataean tombs at Hegra.

name: Sudan
triviaFact: Contains over two hundred steep-sided ancient pyramids in the desert royal necropolis of Meroë, built by the ancient Kingdom of Kush along the upper reaches of the Nile.

name: Senegal
triviaFact: The westernmost mainland territory of the continent, featuring the striking pink waters of Lake Retba and the historical colonial slave depot on Gorée Island.

name: Singapore
triviaFact: A high-density island city-state at the southern tip of the Malay Peninsula, celebrated for futuristic towering Supertrees at Gardens by the Bay and hawker street cuisine.

name: South Georgia
officialName: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands
triviaFact: A southern polar sanctuary of glaciated peaks and fjords where explorer Ernest Shackleton is buried at Grytviken, hosting millions of breeding king penguins and fur seals.

name: Svalbard and Jan Mayen
triviaFact: A High Arctic wilderness where polar bears outnumber people, housing the Global Seed Vault deep within permafrost sandstone to safeguard the future of world agriculture.

name: Solomon Islands
triviaFact: Features Marovo Lagoon, the largest saltwater lagoon in the world bounded by double barrier reefs, alongside submerged World War II shipwrecks in Ironbottom Sound.

name: Sierra Leone
triviaFact: Its historic coastal capital was established in 1792 by liberated enslaved people under the shade of a legendary cotton tree, fringed by white Atlantic palm beaches.

name: El Salvador
triviaFact: The smallest continental mainland territory in the Americas, nicknamed the Land of Volcanoes for its chain of twenty active cones, renowned surf breaks, and pupusa cuisine.

name: San Marino
triviaFact: The world's oldest surviving sovereign republic, founded in 301 AD on the three fortification towers of Mount Titano, governed by two co-equal Captains Regent.

name: Somalia
triviaFact: Boasts the longest oceanic coastline on the African mainland, celebrated for the ancient rock art paintings of Laas Geel depicting domestic cattle ceremonies.

name: Saint Pierre and Miquelon
officialName: Overseas Collectivity of Saint-Pierre and Miquelon
triviaFact: The final remnant of the former colonial empire of New France in North America, anchored off Newfoundland where cobblestones and baguettes meet subarctic fogs.

name: Serbia
triviaFact: Positioned at the confluence of the Sava and Danube rivers below the Kalemegdan fortress, celebrated for medieval Orthodox monasteries adorned with luminous Nemanjic-era frescoes.

name: South Sudan
triviaFact: The newest internationally recognized sovereign nation, home to the vast Sudd wetland swamp along the White Nile where massive wildlife antelope migrations traverse seasonal plains.

name: São Tomé and Príncipe
officialName: Democratic Republic of São Tomé and Príncipe
aliases: República Democrática de São Tomé e Príncipe
triviaFact: An equatorial volcanic island paradise crowned by the needle-like phonolite rock peak of Cão Grande rising dramatically through misty cloud forests.

name: Suriname
triviaFact: The only sovereign nation outside Europe where Dutch is the official language, blanketed by over ninety percent virgin tropical canopy sheltering Maroon cultural heritage.

name: Slovakia
triviaFact: Has the highest concentration of castles and châteaux per capita in the world, framed by the jagged granite peaks of the High Tatras and subterranean ice caves.

name: Slovenia
triviaFact: The emerald Alpine country that gave the geological term 'karst' to the world, featuring Postojna Cave's endemic olm salamanders and a picturesque tear-shaped island on Lake Bled.

name: Sweden
triviaFact: Home to the historic awarding of Nobel Prizes, the intact seventeenth-century salvaged warship Vasa, and thousands of granite islands in the Baltic archipelago.

name: Eswatini
triviaFact: One of the world's last absolute monarchies, celebrated for vibrant cultural ceremonies like the Umhlanga reed dance and ancient iron ore mining at Ngwenya.

name: Sint Maarten
triviaFact: Occupies the southern half of a dual-nation island, world-famous for Maho Beach where jet airliners roar meters over sunbathers on final approach.

name: Seychelles
triviaFact: An archipelago of 115 islands boasting the prehistoric Vallée de Mai palm forest, where the colossal double-lobed coco de mer seed grows wild amidst pink granite boulders.

name: Syria
triviaFact: Features the colonnaded ruins of ancient Palmyra in the desert and Crac des Chevaliers, one of the best-preserved medieval Crusader stone castles in the world.

name: Turks and Caicos Islands
triviaFact: Surrounded by one of the planet's most extensive coral reef systems, welcoming migrating humpback pods each winter along the deep Columbus Passage.

name: Chad
triviaFact: Known as the Dead Heart of Africa, home to the towering volcanic caldera of Emi Koussi in the Tibesti Mountains and the sandstone labyrinth arches of the Ennedi Plateau.

name: Togo
triviaFact: A narrow coastal nation preserving the UNESCO-listed fortress-like two-story mud tower houses of Koutammakou, built by the Batammariba people.

name: Thailand
triviaFact: The only Southeast Asian country to never fall under European colonial rule, renowned for gilded Buddhist wats, limestone karst sea islands, and vibrant street markets.

name: Tajikistan
triviaFact: Over ninety percent mountainous territory traversed by the legendary Pamir Highway across the Roof of the World, home to Fedchenko, the longest glacier outside the polar realms.

name: Tokelau
triviaFact: Three coral atolls with no airports or deepwater harbors, generating nearly one hundred percent of their daily electricity directly from photovoltaic solar power grids.

name: Turkmenistan
triviaFact: Dominated by the Karakum Desert, famous for the glowing natural gas fiery crater known as the Gates of Hell and white marble neoclassical architecture in its capital.

name: Timor-Leste
triviaFact: The first new sovereign state of the twenty-first century, crowned by rugged mist-shrouded peaks and the coral reefs of the Coral Triangle teeming with rare marine life.

name: Tonga
triviaFact: The only sovereign indigenous monarchy in the Pacific to never lose its constitutional self-governance to a foreign power, celebrated for Mapu 'a Vaea coastal blowholes.

name: Trinidad and Tobago
triviaFact: The creative crucible that birthed the steelpan—the only acoustic musical instrument invented in the twentieth century—alongside the natural wonder of Pitch Lake.

name: Tunisia
triviaFact: The ancient realm of Carthage containing the colossal Roman amphitheater of El Jem and troglodyte cave dwellings in Matmata immortalized in cinematic history.

name: Türkiye
triviaFact: A transcontinental crossway spanning the Bosphorus, famous for the surreal fairy chimneys of Cappadocia, hot springs of Pamukkale, and the ancient dome of Hagia Sophia.

name: Tuvalu
triviaFact: A narrow necklace of nine coral atolls rising barely four meters above the Pacific, widely known for leasing its popular two-letter country-code internet domain.

name: Taiwan
triviaFact: A crescent island defined by towering marble walls in Taroko Gorge, semiconductor innovation, and lantern-lit night markets serving soup dumplings and bubble tea.

name: Tanzania
triviaFact: Crowned by the snow-capped peak of Mount Kilimanjaro, the highest point in Africa, overlooking the vast wildlife herds of the Serengeti and the volcanic Ngorongoro Crater.

name: Uganda
triviaFact: Acclaimed as the Pearl of Africa, where thunderous Murchison Falls squeezes the Nile through a seven-meter gorge beside the snow-peaked Rwenzori Mountains.

name: Ukraine
triviaFact: Known as the breadbasket of Europe for its fertile black chornozem soils, boasting the golden onion domes of Pechersk Lavra and the grand State Opera in Lviv.

name: United States Minor Outlying Islands
aliases: Baker, Howland, Jarvis, Johnston, Kingman, Midway, Palmyra, Wake, Navassa
triviaFact: Scattered unpopulated coral atolls and guano preserves designated as marine national monuments, hosting millions of nesting seabirds across isolated maritime zones.

name: Uruguay
triviaFact: Pioneered constitutional secularism and universal suffrage in the region, generating nearly all of its national electrical grid from clean wind and hydroelectric power.

name: United States
triviaFact: Contains the planet's first dedicated national park with its concentration of geothermal geysers, alongside the carved depths of the mile-deep Grand Canyon.

name: Uzbekistan
triviaFact: A doubly landlocked Central Asian crossroad adorned with the turquoise majolica domes and soaring minarets of historic Silk Road oasis cities like Samarkand and Bukhara.

name: Vatican City
triviaFact: The smallest independent state in the world by area and population, completely enclaved within Rome, housing Michelangelo's Sistine Chapel ceiling and Saint Peter's Basilica.

name: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
triviaFact: An arc of thirty-two idyllic isles and cays crowned by La Soufrière volcano, sheltering the turquoise lagoons and sea turtle sanctuaries of Tobago Cays.

name: Venezuela
triviaFact: Features the world's tallest uninterrupted waterfall dropping 979 meters from the tabletop summit of Auyán-tepui, alongside the Catatumbo atmospheric lightning phenomenon.

name: British Virgin Islands
triviaFact: Renowned for The Baths on Virgin Gorda, where colossal granite boulders form sheltered sea caves and natural tidal pools along sparkling sands.

name: United States Virgin Islands
officialName: Virgin Islands of the United States
triviaFact: Former Danish sugarcane trade hub known for emerald hill slopes falling to Trunk Bay's underwater snorkel trails and historic stone windmill ruins.

name: Vietnam
aliases: Cộng hòa Xã hội chủ nghĩa Việt Nam
triviaFact: Features the otherworldly emerald waters and emerald-topped limestone karst pillars of Ha Long Bay, alongside the cavernous underground chambers of Son Doong cave.

name: Vanuatu
triviaFact: Birthplace of land diving (Naghol) on Pentecost Island—the spiritual ancestor of modern bungee jumping—shadowed by the glowing, active magma pit of Mount Yasur.

name: Wallis and Futuna
officialName: Territory of the Wallis and Futuna Islands
triviaFact: A French South Pacific territory that uniquely preserves three traditional recognized Polynesian customary kingdoms alongside the circular crater waters of Lake Lalolalo.

name: Samoa
triviaFact: Governed by a 3,000-year-old traditional communal code of customs, famed for the dramatic natural sea swimming grotto of To-Sua Ocean Trench on Upolu.

name: Yemen
triviaFact: Known as Arabia Felix in antiquity, home to the multi-story ancient mudbrick skyscrapers of Shibam—the 'Manhattan of the Desert'—and dragon blood trees on Socotra.

name: South Africa
triviaFact: Features the flat-topped sandstone summit of Table Mountain overlooking two oceans, Kruger National Park's diverse ecosystems, and three designated constitutional capital cities.

name: Zambia
triviaFact: Shares the thunderous cataract of Victoria Falls, locally known as Mosi-oa-Tunya, plunging over one hundred meters into the winding basalt gorges of the Zambezi.

name: Zimbabwe
triviaFact: Named after a medieval stone citadel featuring mortarless dry-stone granite walls and conical towers constructed between the eleventh and fifteenth centuries.
